analysis.file_name: Bernstein - Data Center Pipeline Probabilities - Gigawatts versus Bragawatts - what's really getting built (Oct'26).pdf
analysis.title: Data Center Pipeline Probabilities: Gigawatts versus Bragawatts - what's really getting built (Oct '26)
key_insights: Of 586GW of North American data center pipeline capacity in Bernstein's October data, 34% (199GW) is judged credible. The completion rate was 33% in June and 35% in August, so it is stable while the absolute credible GW keeps rising.
Credible capacity rose to 199GW in October from 170GW in August and 136GW in July. Dataset capacity rose to 586GW from 488GW in August and 411GW in July.
Haircuts to the pipeline total roughly 387GW. Stage is the largest (~198GW), then tenant (~112GW), developer/company (~48GW) and state (~28GW).

By stage, announced projects are 85% of the dataset but have a ~25% build probability. Under construction is 15% of the dataset, with an 86% probability, and is 38% of the credible pipeline. Land bank is ~2GW at ~43%.
The top 10 developers account for ~57% of credible capacity. Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Meta together are ~39% of credible MW (78GW). Sixteen developers hold a perfect 5.0 credibility score.
By developer type, hyperscaler self-build has 84GW credible of 111GW (75%) and colocation has 67GW of 108GW (62%). Miner pivots (24%), neoclouds (29%) and others (11%) are much lower.

Hyperscaler self-build is ~41% of credible builds (82GW). Projects with no disclosed tenant are ~43% of the credible pipeline. OpenAI-linked demand (5.8GW credible) is the second-largest named counterparty behind AWS (9.2GW).

Four developers are building for the Oracle + OpenAI combination: Vantage (~1.9GW), Related Digital (~1.0GW), BorderPlex (~620MW) and Crusoe (~210MW). About 0.9GW is already live at Crusoe's Abilene campus.

Following the Nov 3 elections, three large data center states (TX, GA, OH) elected governors who campaigned on moratoria. Bernstein now haircuts announced and land-banked capacity in eight states, up from six in July. It expects delays more than cancellations.

~68% of forward credible pipeline capacity is in the 13 states Bernstein flags as risky. Texas is the most penalized state at a ~12GW impact (150GW in the database, 43GW credible). Virginia is second at ~6GW and Pennsylvania third at ~3GW.

Texas and Pennsylvania move to the 0.70 multiplier floor. Georgia sees the largest single move. Ohio, Oregon and Indiana also tighten, and Maryland and Louisiana enter the haircut table for the first time. Whether Texas warrants a tier below 0.70 is left open.

In Texas, 21GW (16GW credible) is under construction and grandfathered. Of the not-yet-started announced capacity, 18GW total / 5GW credible is slated for 2028 (most at risk) and 39GW / 8GW for 2029. The tax incentives remain.

Georgia's Public Service Commission flipped 3-2 Democratic. The existing approvals, including OpenAI's 3.2GW contract, are done. The new majority can reach Georgia Power's next capacity request (filed mid-2027) and the 2028 rate case. 87% of Georgia's pre-construction credible capacity is dated 2029 or later.

In Ohio, local bans passed in at least ten towns. A quick read suggests ~3GW of credible capacity was zoned out, but the bans bind on only ~1.1GW. Projects tend to move to the next town. A Nov 10 St. Clair Township hearing could put AWS Trenton (~1GW credible) into the binding column.

Behind-the-meter (BTM) power added 22.5GW to the pipeline in October, bringing the BTM pipeline to 231GW from 185GW in August. Credible BTM is only 47GW, so its credible share fell from 23% to about a fifth. BTM is 28% of stranded capacity.

Neoclouds are the most reliant on BTM (62% of their pipeline), but only 21% of neocloud BTM capacity is credible, against 73% for hyperscaler self-build and 55% for colos. Only 4% of operating capacity uses BTM, against 17% of capacity under construction and 43% of announced capacity.

Credibility by market tier: Tier 1 major metro 39%, Tier 2 40%, Tier 3 35%, Tier 4 rural 31%. Major metros have the highest build costs ($12-15B per GW) and the longest power delays (4-7 years). Rural markets cost $7-9B per GW with power in 1-3 years.

Tenant credit is bifurcating. HUMAIN, Lambda and Cohere were upgraded. OpenAI was trimmed after cutting its funding target to $20B from ~$30B. Oracle's multiplier was cut from 0.80 to 0.75 after the Project Jupiter force majeure notice and Moody's negative outlook. TensorWave was cut after its Fermi lease missed closing.

Developer score changes: Crusoe's capital score rose 4 to 5 and TeraWulf's power score rose 3 to 4. Nscale's offtake score fell 5 to 4 and Fermi America's fell 3 to 2. Crusoe, Sabey and Serverfarm were upgraded on new financing.

O'Leary Ventures (15GW announced, ~3% credible, score 0.35) and Joule Capital Partners (11.7GW announced, 9% credible) are the lowest-credibility large developers. Vermaland's 2.2GW is now cancelled after Pinal County rejected the rezoning 4-1.

Top picks are EQIX (Outperform, PT $1,270) and DLR (Outperform, PT $226) in data centers. In US machinery and electricals the picks are PWR ($804), ETN ($534), HUBB ($560), FPS ($48) and LGN ($103), all Outperform. CRWV is rated Underperform with a $54 target.

sector_views.rationale: EQIX and DLR have the most credible developer footprints in major metros and diversified pipelines.
PWR, ETN, HUBB, FPS and LGN are rated Outperform and expected to benefit from short and long-term data center tailwinds.
Only 29% of neocloud capacity and 24% of miner-pivot capacity is credible, they are the most reliant on BTM power, and their tenant multipliers are low.

crypto_views: Miner pivots have 35GW in the dataset and 8GW (24%) credible. Core Scientific and Galaxy carry 0.40 tenant multipliers. TeraWulf's power score was raised from 3 to 4, and Cipher Mining and Galaxy appear among the 10 lowest-credibility developers.
risk_factors: State regulatory risk after the Nov 3 elections: governors in TX, GA and OH campaigned on moratoria, and Bernstein now haircuts eight states. It expects delay more than cancellation.

Tenant credit risk: OpenAI cut its funding round target to $20B from ~$30B, Oracle issued a Project Jupiter force majeure notice and Moody's kept a negative outlook, and S&P has a negative outlook on Meta.

Individual project decisions: Amazon withdrew from a 427-acre Ashburn project, Microsoft exited Loughton, and Union County, PA halted PNK Group's substation build. Bernstein says these do not change hyperscaler credit.

Behind-the-meter power is rising but credible capacity is not keeping pace. BTM is 28% of cancelled, withdrawn and delayed capacity, and the largest October cancellation was the 4.0GW DCIP De Soto campus.
Local bans can bind faster than state action, for example in Ohio. Disclosed tenant data is the weakest part of the dataset because contracts are not always announced.
Neocloud credit shocks, and developers with announced-only pipelines such as O'Leary Ventures, Joule and Fermi America, are likely to deliver far less than their headline GW.

tension_points.bull_case: Most credible capacity is still very likely to be built. 21GW in Texas is grandfathered, the tax incentives remain, and Georgia's approvals are in place. Ohio bans bind on only ~1.1GW, and projects tend to move to the next town.
tension_points.bear_case: Governors elected in TX, GA and OH campaigned on moratoria. Texas is already at the 0.70 floor, Georgia's PSC flipped Democratic, and Bernstein now haircuts eight states instead of six. Delay risk is highest for 2028-2029 Texas capacity.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If St. Clair Township adopts its ban, AWS Trenton (~1GW credible) moves into the binding column and Ohio becomes a much more interesting story. Bernstein also asks whether Texas should move to a tier below 0.70.

tension_points.bull_case: BTM added 22.5GW in October and the pipeline reached 231GW. 17% of capacity under construction will use BTM.
tension_points.bear_case: Credible BTM rose only ~5GW to 47GW. Only 21% of neocloud BTM capacity is credible, and BTM is 28% of stranded capacity.

theme_stances.key_argument: Only about a third of the 586GW pipeline is credible, because stage, tenant, developer and state haircuts remove most announced capacity.
theme_stances.evidence: we're not giving full credit for press releases and PowerPoints

theme_stances.key_argument: The elections raise delay risk in eight states, but Bernstein does not expect most projects to be canceled.
theme_stances.evidence: Our view is still not that most of those projects will be canceled
